title: Careers in IT and Computer Applications
content:
Chapter 7: Careers in IT and Areas of Application

1. Careers in Information Technology

Hardware-Related Careers

  • Computer Engineer: Designs and develops computer hardware components.
  • Network Engineer: Installs, maintains and troubleshoots networks.
  • Hardware Technician: Repairs and maintains computer hardware.
  • Electronics Engineer: Designs electronic circuits and systems.

Software-Related Careers

  • Software Developer/Programmer: Writes and tests software applications.
  • Systems Analyst: Analyses existing systems and designs improvements.
  • Database Administrator (DBA): Manages and maintains databases.
  • Web Developer: Designs and builds websites and web applications.
  • Cybersecurity Analyst: Protects computer systems from attacks.
  • IT Project Manager: Plans and manages IT projects.

2. Areas of Application of Computers

AreaApplications
Educatione-Learning platforms, computer-based testing, virtual classrooms
Medicine/HealthPatient records, diagnostic imaging, robotic surgery
Business/CommerceOnline banking, e-commerce, payroll, inventory
EntertainmentVideo games, digital music, streaming, animation
CommunicationEmail, social media, video calls, instant messaging
Science & ResearchSimulations, data analysis, weather forecasting
TransportGPS navigation, traffic control, autopilot systems
GovernmentE-voting, national databases, tax collection

title: Computer Ergonomics and Health Hazards
content:
Computer Ergonomics and Health Hazards

Ergonomics is the science of designing equipment, systems, and workplaces to fit the people who use them, improving comfort, efficiency, and safety.

Computer Health Hazards

DisorderCauseBody Part Affected
Repetitive Strain Injury (RSI)Repetitive movements (e.g., typing, clicking)Wrists, hands, fingers
Carpal Tunnel SyndromeProlonged use of keyboard/mouseWrist, hand
Eye Strain (CVS)Prolonged screen useEyes
Back/Neck PainPoor posture, wrong chair heightBack, neck, spine
HeadachesScreen glare, eye strainHead

Safety Precautions (Ergonomic Solutions)

  • Adjust chair height so feet are flat on floor.
  • Place monitor at eye level, arm's length away.
  • Use wrist rests when typing.
  • Take regular breaks (at least every hour).
  • Use anti-glare screen filters.
  • Keep cables tidy to prevent trip hazards.
  • Ensure good room lighting.
  • Use adjustable desks and chairs.

Assistive Technology for Social Inclusion

Assistive technology is any technology that helps people with disabilities use computers and access information.
  • Screen reader: Software that reads screen content aloud (e.g., JAWS) – for visually impaired users.
  • Braille keyboard: Keyboard with Braille characters.
  • Voice recognition software: Control computer by voice.
  • Eye-tracking device: Control computer using eye movements.
  • Screen magnifier: Enlarges screen content.
  • Switch access: Allows users with limited motor skills to operate computers with a single button.

title: Computer Ethics and Legislation
content:
Computer Ethics and Legislation

I. Computer Ethics

Computer ethics is a branch of practical philosophy dealing with how computing professionals should make decisions regarding professional and social conduct.

Fundamental Principles of Ethics

  • Honesty: Be truthful in all professional activities.
  • Fairness: Treat all people equally and without bias.
  • Privacy: Respect individuals' personal information.
  • Responsibility: Be accountable for your actions.
  • Non-maleficence: Do not use technology to harm others.

Professional Codes of Ethics

  • BCS Code of Ethics: Serve public interest; maintain professional competence; act with integrity.
  • ACM Code of Ethics: Contribute to society; avoid harm; be honest and trustworthy.
  • IEEE Code of Ethics: Hold safety paramount; act in the public interest; be honest.

II. Legislation (Laws)

ActPurposeKey Points
Data Protection ActProtect personal dataData must be accurate, secure, used for intended purpose; individuals have right to see their data.
Computer Misuse ActCombat computer crimeMakes unauthorised access, modification of computer material, and use of computers for fraud illegal.
Copyright, Design and Patent ActProtect intellectual propertyMakes it illegal to copy, distribute, or use software, music, or other creative works without permission.
Health and Safety ActProtect workersEmployers must provide safe working conditions, including safe use of computers and VDUs.

III. Computer Crime

CrimeDescription
HackingUnauthorised access to computer systems
PhishingUsing fake emails/websites to steal personal information
Identity TheftUsing someone else's personal information fraudulently
CyberbullyingUsing the internet to harass or threaten others
Software PiracyCopying or distributing software without a licence
Invasion of PrivacyCollecting or misusing personal data without consent

title: Social and Economic Impacts of Computers
content:
Social and Economic Impacts of Computers

Positive Impacts

  • Employment: Created many new types of jobs in IT sector.
  • Communication: Instant worldwide communication.
  • Education: Access to vast information resources globally.
  • Healthcare: Improved diagnosis, treatment, and patient care.
  • Productivity: Tasks done faster and more accurately.
  • Business: Global trade, e-commerce, online banking.
  • Entertainment: New forms of entertainment – streaming, gaming.

Negative Impacts

  • Unemployment: Automation has replaced some human jobs.
  • Privacy concerns: Personal data collection and misuse.
  • Digital divide: Unequal access to technology creates inequality.
  • Cybercrime: Increased opportunities for fraud, theft, hacking.
  • Health problems: Eye strain, RSI, sedentary lifestyle, addiction.
  • Spread of misinformation: False information spreads quickly online.
  • Environmental impact: e-Waste, energy consumption of data centres.

Impacts of Social Networks

Positive: Reconnect with old friends; share ideas and information; support communities; marketing for businesses; raise awareness for social causes.

Negative: Cyberbullying; addiction; privacy invasion; spread of misinformation; reduced face-to-face interaction; security risks.
